# Rivalry in Canton: The Control of Russell and Co, 1838-1840 and the Founding of Augustine Heard and Co. Paperback – 1 Nov. 2006 

 by Tim Sturgis (Author) 

 For American merchants in the 1830s, the tea trade with China was perhaps the most profitable and most sought after of all. The 'House' of Russell & Co, largely run by Bostonians, was the leading American firm in Canton at the time. This book tells the story of two Boston merchants, a Forbes and a Coolidge, each intent on becoming the senior partner of the 'House', and consequently of making their fortunes. The story starts with the departure of Joseph Coolidge from Boston in 1835 on his way back to Canton, where he had been a partenr of Russell & Co since 1834. It ends at the beginning of 1840, when Coolidge is ejected fromn the House, being replaced by Robert Bennet Forbes, who usurped Coolidge's place; in response Coolidge founds the new 'House' of Augustine Heard & Co, to compete with the older firm. Both firms flourish until the 1870s. The struggle between Coolidge and Forbes is set against the ending of the trading monopoly of the EastIndia Company in 1834, the growing friction caused ny the rapid expansion of the opium trade which resulted from this, and which finally led to the Opium War of 1840. It ranges fromn Canton and the Co-Hong merchants, to the Boston merchants, and to London where money was raised through Barings Bank and the tea was sold. It describes the colourful and independent characters involved and their wives, all of whon had a role to play. It describes the history, the workings and the intemational ramifications of the America-China trade.
